title: Secure Pathways Terraform module for private deployment security controls
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a reusable Terraform module (Secure Pathways) that encapsulates Redwood's recommended security controls for Private/VPC deployments. The module will provision security groups, network ACLs, private hosted zones (Route53 or cloud equivalent), and an opinionated egress policy layer (allow-lists, outbound proxy integration, and deny-lists). It should be consumable by Private deployment automation (both VPC and on-prem variants), support safe upgrades, provide health checks, and expose telemetry for Console observability. Focus is on a composable, policy-driven module that can be configured per-environment (prod/staging/dev) and per-customer. Avoid duplicating existing hardening modules by providing higher-level orchestration and verification steps that integrate with our rollout and upgrade tooling.
tasks: Design module schema and configuration flags (allow_list, deny_list, proxy_integration, private_dns_enabled, acl_mode)
Implement security groups with least-privilege egress rules and tags for cost/traceability
Implement network ACLs with stateful/edge guards and fail-safe default deny
Add private DNS support with option to create a hosted zone and conditional forwarding rules
Implement egress policy primitives: allow-list mode, deny-list mode, and proxy passthrough
Add health check resources (synthetic egress probes, DNS resolution checks) and integrate with our metrics exporter
Write automated acceptance tests using terratest and CI pipeline validation
Add upgrade hooks and migration notes for existing customers (idempotent changes only)
Document module usage, examples for day-0 and day-2 operations, and example policies
Create a minimal example repo and sample configs for Dedicated vs Private on-prem
acceptance_criteria: Module publishes to internal Terraform registry and can be consumed with a single module block
Default configuration does not permit wide-open egress; non-blocking allow-list opt-in is explicit
Health checks surface failures as metrics in Console and produce clear remediation steps
Automated tests pass in CI across AWS and GCP templates used by Private deployments
Upgrade path documented and tested: existing stacks can opt into new ACL rules without downtime
Security review completed and findings triaged with accompanying tickets
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature branch behind feature flag. 2) Publish module to internal registry and tag release. 3) Run canary in staging account with dedicated test app and monitor health checks for 48 hours. 4) Roll out to a small set of pilot customers (3) with SRE monitoring. 5) Gradual adoption across remaining Private/Dedicated deployments; post-rollout audit and cleanup of deprecated hardening modules.

notes: Trade-offs: prefer explicit allow-lists to maximize safety, but provide helper tooling to generate allow-lists from observed traffic during pilot. Avoid bundling provider-specific assumptions; use provider-agnostic naming and conditional blocks for AWS/GCP/OnPrem differences.
implementation_guidance: When upgrading existing customers, use a phased approach: 1) deploy module in monitoring-only mode (no changes to rules), 2) enable audit logs and synthetic checks, 3) progressively apply restrictive rules under a canary tag. Keep resource addresses stable to prevent replacement.
